question_candidates.stop_reason: Source investigation answers the reachability premise negatively for the fault model this code implements, so the Candidate is explained rather than escalated. handleCommit's NOOP-repropose branch dereferences inst.lb.clientProposals with no nil check (epaxos/epaxos.go:1092), and newInstanceDefault leaves lb nil, so the dereference would panic if it were reached with a placeholder. But the branch is guarded by commit.Replica == r.Id, i.e. the receiver is the row owner of the instance, and the row owner is the only creator of entries in its own row: handlePropose allocates into r.crtInstance[r.Id] (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749) and startPhase1 installs InstanceSpace[replica][instance] together with a fresh LeaderBookkeeping (lb) before bcastPreAccept (epaxos/epaxos.go:751-779). Every other path that can produce a Commit for row R with a NOOP command goes through a recovery leader's startPhase1(preply.Replica, ...) (epaxos/epaxos.go:1307-1312), which only ever recovers an instance (R,i) that already existed, and an instance (R,i) can only originate from R's own proposal because handlePropose always uses r.Id. crtInstance[R] is likewise only advanced together with creating the entry. So in a crash-free execution the receiver's own-row entry always has non-nil lb, and the nil-lb placeholder state on one's own row requires the row owner to have lost its own instance, which is the durability/restart path (Durable false, replay unread) rather than a legal history of the modelled faults. The missing guard is a real latent robustness gap and I keep it visible as a remaining item, but I do not claim a reachable defect.

question_candidates.stop_reason: Source investigation answers the remaining discriminator as a bounded delay rather than an unbounded stall, so the Candidate is explained by an existing mechanism instead of escalated. The gap itself is real and now recorded in the map: a higher-ballot AcceptReply is dropped at the equality gate (epaxos/epaxos.go:1024-1026) so handleAcceptReply never counts a nack or calls makeBallot/bcastPrepare. But non-completion at a ballot is not final for the instance. Every replica's executeCommands loop re-examines each row from ExecedUpTo+1 and, when a head instance stays non-executable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD, enqueues instancesToRecover for that instance (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-435); the local loop then runs startRecoveryForInstance, which rebuilds the instance bookkeeping and calls makeBallot then bcastPrepare (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1169). makeBallot chooses the recovering replica's own ballot slot, and for a replica that is not the row owner it uses r.Id + N, while an IsLeader additionally raises past maxRecvBallot (epaxos/epaxos.go:439-451), so a recovery attempt at an equal-or-higher ballot is available without the Accept-path escalation. Acceptors then adopt that prepare ballot (handlePrepare, epaxos/epaxos.go:1183-1187) and handlePrepareReply rebuilds the instance and re-enters Accept or phase 1 (epaxos/epaxos.go:1204-1314). So the missing Accept-path nack costs at most the timer interval and a recovery round, not permanent stalling. I keep visible that this is a liveness/latency argument, not a proof of bounded latency, and that IsLeader gating and the non-leader ballot range bound how much a single recovery can raise the ballot.

question_candidates.stop_reason: Source investigation answers the pairing premise negatively for this server, so the Candidate is explained rather than escalated. The client's positional pairing would be wrong only if replies arrived in an order different from the requests, but on this server they cannot for a single client. runSingleClient sets Leaderless=true and Fast=false for epaxos, so every proposal from one client is sent to ClosestId (client/client.go:175-196) and B-CLIENT-ISSUE's SendWrite/SendRead/SendScan therefore land on one replica; handlePropose assigns each batch to that replica's own row and allocates consecutive instances (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749). Dreply is true (replica/replica.go:94), so the coordinator does not answer at commit (the !Dreply branches at epaxos/epaxos.go:931 and 1044 are skipped) and the only reply path is execution, where shouldRespond replies per command in w.Cmds order (epaxos/exec.go:119-140). Within the proposing replica's row, execution is head-driven: executeCommands walks each row from ExecedUpTo+1 and stops at the first non-executable instance (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-435), and a same-row instance cannot be a dependency of an earlier one, so same-row instances are never mutual SCC members and are emitted in increasing instance order; a batched proposal replies for cmds[0..k] in order. So arrival order equals request order for one client, and the missing identity check has no observable consequence under the modelled leaderless client. I keep the gap visible as a latent contract question (it would matter for a client that talks to more than one replica or if replies were emitted per-RPC rather than at execution).

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, carried by bal/vbal (F-BALLOT). A coordinator acquires the trial ballot in startPhase1; acceptors only accept a ballot >= their stored bal, so a higher-ballot message transfers authority away from a stalled coordinator. Recovery (A3) raises the ballot via makeBallot, issues Prepare, and reconstructs the instance's (vbal, status, seq, deps) from a slow quorum, then re-uses the formation paths. Established COMMITTED instances are not re-decided (handleCommit returns early), and CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix to acceptors and coordinators.

connection.explanation: Recovery and formation share the same per-instance facts: a recovering coordinator rebuilds F-PREACCEPT-STATE from the highest-VBallot Prepare replies and then either takes the slow Accept path, TryPreAccept (guarded by findPreAcceptConflicts), or restarts phase1 with a NOOP/old command. Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. Thus old requests survive via lb.clientProposals carried into recovery and re-proposed on a NOOP commit, and established decisions constrain all later formation by fixing (Cmds, Seq, Deps) and the contiguous committed prefix.

selections.rationale: First pass on the EPaxos replica. Traced both core lines (A1 qualified support for decision formation; A2 per-instance ballot/authority transitions) plus the A3 recovery, A5 execution, A6 persistence and A7 client paths that connect them, and wrote a usable partial map in map.json. Formation: handlePropose allocates an own-row instance, startPhase1 pre-accepts with conflict-derived (seq,deps), and handlePreAcceptReply fast-commits on an agreeing fast quorum on the initial ballot (COMMITTED) or falls back to Accept needing a majority. Context/authority: authority is per instance via bal/vbal; acceptors reject lower ballots, makeBallot raises the ballot, and recovery issues Prepare then either accept-commits, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase1 from the highest-VBallot replies. Connection: recovery rebuilds the same F-PREACCEPT-STATE facts the formation path consumes, CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix, and execution consumes only the committed dependency graph, so old client proposals are carried through lb.clientProposals and re-proposed on a NOOP commit. Several local anomalies were recorded as sourced unknowns rather than defects: the handlePreAccept Status>=ACCEPTED & Cmds==nil branch writes InstanceSpace[LeaderId] instead of the instance being handled; the subcase-3 and subcase-4 guards in handlePrepareReply are textually identical; and the notInQuorum loop in handleTryPreAcceptReply indexes possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] instead of possibleQuorum[q]. None is yet grounded as an applicable violated responsibility.

feedback.answered: Core relationships recorded. A1: qualified support for decision formation is a coordinator-local sequence of startPhase1 (PREACCEPTED with conflict-derived seq/deps) plus PreAcceptReply aggregation; the decision is COMMITTED only when a fast quorum agrees, the trial ballot is the initial ballot, and (N>7) committed deps are present, otherwise the Accept phase resolves by majority. A2: authority is a per-instance ballot; acceptors only accept ballot >= stored bal, a coordinator that observes a higher ballot raises its own via makeBallot and issues Prepare, and recovery reconstructs (vbal,status,seq,deps) from a slow quorum before re-entering accept or phase1. Connection: recovery reproduces the same per-instance pre-accept facts the formation path consumes, the committed prefix (CommittedUpTo) and idempotent handleCommit bound re-decisions, and execution consumes only the committed dependency graph, with old client proposals carried in lb.clientProposals.
remaining: Whether the handlePreAccept branch that writes InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][preAccept.Instance].Cmds can ever run with LeaderId != Replica, and if so whether it mutates a wrong or nil slot (safety-relevant).
Whether the identical class-3/class-4 conditions in handlePrepareReply make the TryPreAccept recovery sub-case unreachable, and if so what a concurrent-conflict recovery would do instead.
Whether the notInQuorum loop in handleTryPreAcceptReply (always testing possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId]) can let a real deferred recovery cycle through.
Membership (A4) and thrifty/quorum-file selection: which quorum thresholds are active at runtime, since the fast/slow commit predicates depend on FastQuorumSize/SlowQuorumSize.
Durability (A6): the restart replay path and the apparent bal/vbal byte-offset overlap in recordInstanceMetadata are unread.

formation.explanation: A coordinator pre-accepts a batch in its own row (B-PROPOSE/B-PHASE1), then aggregates PreAcceptReply: if the fast quorum agrees on seq/deps (allEqual), the trial ballot is the initial ballot, and (for N>7) all committed deps are present, it fast-commits; otherwise it enters Accept and needs a majority. Both paths produce a concrete per-instance (Cmds, Seq, Deps) recorded as F-DECISION/F-COMMITTED and propagated by Commit.

context.explanation: Authority is per instance, carried by bal/vbal (F-BALLOT). A coordinator acquires the trial ballot in startPhase1; acceptors only accept a ballot >= their stored bal, so a higher-ballot message transfers authority away from a stalled coordinator. Recovery (A3) raises the ballot via makeBallot, issues Prepare, and reconstructs the instance's (vbal, status, seq, deps) from a slow quorum, then re-uses the formation paths. Established COMMITTED instances are not re-decided (handleCommit returns early), and CommittedUpTo exposes a stable committed prefix to acceptors and coordinators.

connection.explanation: Recovery and formation share the same per-instance facts: a recovering coordinator rebuilds F-PREACCEPT-STATE from the highest-VBallot Prepare replies and then either takes the slow Accept path, TryPreAccept (guarded by findPreAcceptConflicts), or restarts phase1 with a NOOP/old command. Committed support is the boundary: acceptors report CommittedUpTo, handleCommit is idempotent for already-COMMITTED instances, and execution (B-EXEC) consumes only the committed dependency graph. Thus old requests survive via lb.clientProposals carried into recovery and re-proposed on a NOOP commit, and established decisions constrain all later formation by fixing (Cmds, Seq, Deps) and the contiguous committed prefix.

The most concrete sourced discrepancy is that the defer-cycle guard in handleTryPreAcceptReply is inert: lb.possibleQuorum is initialized all-false and only ever assigned false (line 1445-1446), and the notInQuorum loop tests lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] using the constant reply's AcceptorId for every q (line 1461) instead of lb.possibleQuorum[q].
